title: 「WH + to-infinitive 名詞句」
titleEn: Using WH + to-infinitive as a noun phrase

omissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules and Benefits headings are faithful editorial translations.

formula: Subject + verb / phrase + WH-word (+ noun) + to + base verb + other information

formulas.formula: Subject + verb / phrase + WH-word (+ noun) + to + base verb + other information

example: I do not know what to do next.
exampleZh: 我不知道下一步該做甚麼。

examples.en: I do not know what to do next.
examples.zh: 我不知道下一步該做甚麼。

rules.zh: WH + to 通常不是一條獨立問題，而是在完整句子中擔任名詞成分。
rules.en: The WH + to phrase forms part of a larger sentence. It is normally not an independent question, but functions as a noun element within the complete sentence.
examples: I cannot decide where to go.
Please tell me what to bring.

rules.zh: 在 to 後面必須使用動詞原形。
rules.en: Use the base form after to.

rules.zh: 把完整的間接問句縮短為 WH + to 後，不再保留主詞和 should、can 等情態動詞。
rules.en: Do not put a subject or question word order after the WH-word. When a full indirect question is reduced to WH + to, remove the subject and modal verbs such as should or can.

rules.zh: 當說話者需要從幾個已知選項中作出選擇時，常使用： 如果名詞已經非常清楚，也可以省略名詞：
rules.en: Use which + noun + to + base verb when choosing from a limited group of known options. If the noun is already completely clear, it may be omitted.
examples: which + noun + to + base verb which bus to take
I cannot decide which to choose.

rules.zh: 在現代日常英語中，通常使用： 較正式的英語有時使用 whom，但本練習統一使用較自然和常見的 who。
rules.en: Who is common in modern everyday English in forms such as who to ask, who to contact and who to speak to. More formal English sometimes uses whom, but this exercise consistently uses the more natural and common who.

rules.zh: 一般不會說： 應改為完整子句： Whether to 是相關句型，但不屬於本課的 WH + to 練習範圍。
rules.en: Why to is not normally used in this pattern; use a complete clause such as why I should leave instead. Whether to is a related construction but is outside the WH + to practice in this lesson.
examples: I do not know why I should leave.

benefits.zh: 可以縮短較長的間接問句 你不需要重複主詞和 should、can 等字，也可以更直接地表達相同問題。
benefits.en: It shortens a longer indirect question. Instead of repeating the subject and words such as should or can, you can express the same question more directly.
examples: I do not know what to do.

benefits.zh: 幫助你表達決定和不確定的事情 這個句型很適合用來說明你仍未決定地點、時間、人物、方法或選項。
benefits.en: It helps you talk about decisions and uncertainty, especially when a place, time, person, method or option has not yet been decided.
examples: We have not decided where to stay.
She is not sure who to ask.

benefits.zh: 讓指示更容易表達和理解 你可以用這個句型清楚說明某人需要做甚麼、在哪裏做、何時做或如何做。
benefits.en: It makes instructions easier to give and understand by stating clearly what someone needs to do, where or when to do it, or how to do it.
examples: The guide explained where to wait.
The website shows users how to reset their passwords.

benefits.zh: 把相關資料合併成一句 你可以把一條問題和另一句說明合併起來，避免使用太多短句。
benefits.en: It combines related information into one sentence by joining a question to another statement and avoiding too many short sentences.
examples: We need to decide which train to take.

benefits.zh: 提供實用的說話和寫作框架 只要記住以下框架，便可以加入不同內容： 這些框架適合日常對話、學校寫作、工作指示、電郵和報告。
benefits.en: It provides useful speaking and writing frames such as I do not know what to ..., We need to decide where to ..., Please show me how to ... and She is unsure which ... to choose. These patterns suit everyday conversation, school writing, workplace instructions, emails and reports.

sourceOmissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules and Benefits headings are faithful editorial translations.

en: Rewrite each sentence using a WH-word + to + base verb structure.
Preserve the original meaning, subject, tense, objects and other important information.
The first word of each answer has been provided.

答案須保留原句的意思、主詞、時態、受詞及其他重要資料。
每題已提供答案的第一個字。
